field.lat.label: Latitude
field.lat.help: The latitude of the centre of the search, in degrees (WGS84). Example: 49.2320.
field.lon.label: Longitude
field.lon.help: The longitude of the centre of the search, in degrees (WGS84). Example: 19.9817.
field.northing.label: Northing (PL-1992)
field.northing.help: The centre of the search in the Polish grid PL-1992 (EPSG:2180), in metres. Geoportal shows it as X.
field.easting.label: Easting (PL-1992)
field.easting.help: The centre of the search in the Polish grid PL-1992 (EPSG:2180), in metres. Geoportal shows it as Y.
field.radius.label: Search radius
field.radius.help: The search looks for anchors in this circle around the centre. Both anchors of a line are in the circle. A larger circle takes longer and gives more lines.
field.area.label: Area
field.area.help: Searches an area instead of a circle: along cliffs or the coast, an OpenStreetMap area or your file. Both anchors of a line are in the area. The webbing can go out of it.
field.buffer.label: Band width
field.buffer.help: The search area around cliffs, the coast, or the points and lines of your file. Polygons are used as they are. Example: 100 m takes the cliff edge and the ground behind it.
field.within.label: Limit to
field.within.help: The part of the map for "Along cliffs". Give an OpenStreetMap name (e.g. Gozo) or use the map view. Cliffs near the coast of a named island are included.
field.name.label: Search name
field.name.help: The name in your list of searches. Empty: the place name from OpenStreetMap.
field.min_length.label: Shortest line
field.min_length.help: The distance between the anchors. Use the range of lines that you will rig. A narrow range gives a faster search and a clearer map.
field.max_length.label: Longest line
field.max_length.help: The distance between the anchors. Use the range of lines that you will rig. A narrow range gives a faster search and a clearer map.
field.max_anchor_diff_m.label: Anchor height difference
field.max_anchor_diff_m.help: The largest height difference between the two anchors. A line with a large difference is steep and hard to walk. Typical highlines: 10 m or less.
field.max_anchor_diff.label: Anchor height difference, % of length
field.max_anchor_diff.help: The same limit as a part of the line length. Both limits apply. Example: 5 % of a 200 m line is 10 m.
field.max_wall_angle.label: Angle to the wall, at most
field.max_wall_angle.help: How far the line turns from the fall line of the wall at each anchor. 0°: the line goes straight out over the drop. 90°: the line goes along the wall. Use 30–45° for clean exits from a wall.
field.slope_threshold.label: Anchor steepness
field.slope_threshold.help: The terrain must be at least this steep for an anchor. A higher value keeps only edges of walls and gives fewer anchors. Default 45°.
field.min_prominence.label: Prominence of one anchor, at least
field.min_prominence.help: Keeps lines with at least one anchor on a feature that stands out: a tower, a needle, a block. Prominence is the height of the rock above the place where it joins wider ground.
field.min_prominence_both.label: Prominence of both anchors, at least
field.min_prominence_both.help: The same, for both anchors. Use it for lines between two towers.
field.prominence_span.label: Prominence: base width
field.prominence_span.help: Ground wider than this is not part of the anchor's rock. Use a small value (30–50 m) for needles, a large value for big walls.
field.min_drop.label: Drop below both anchors, at least
field.min_drop.help: Both anchors must be this high above the lowest ground near them. It removes anchors on small steps in a slope.
field.drop_radius.label: Drop: measured within
field.drop_radius.help: The distance around each anchor where the search finds the lowest ground for the drop.
field.nmpt.label: Trees and buildings
field.nmpt.help: Checks the clearance above trees and buildings too. "Mark" shows such lines in orange. "Remove" deletes them from the result. "Do not check" is faster.
field.high_above.label: Counts as high from
field.high_above.help: From this height above the ground, a part of the line is "high". The result shows the high part of each line in %.
field.min_height.label: Highest point above the ground, at least
field.min_height.help: Keeps lines that get this high above the ground at one point or more. The height is measured below the sagged webbing with the walker on it.
field.min_mean_height.label: Mean height above the ground, at least
field.min_mean_height.help: Keeps lines that are this high on average along their length.
field.min_high_share.label: High part of the line, at least
field.min_high_share.help: Keeps lines that are higher than "Counts as high from" along this part of their length. Example: 70 % for lines with exposure from end to end.
field.model.label: Clearance model
field.model.help: How the search calculates the lowest point of the webbing. "Simple formula" is fast and safe for most lines. "Sag estimate" calculates the sag from the rigging values below and adds the leash fall space.
field.pretension.label: Pretension
field.pretension.help: The tension in the main line before anybody walks it.
field.stretch.label: Webbing stretch at 10 kN
field.stretch.help: How much the webbing gets longer at 10 kN, from its data sheet. Polyester ≈ 1–3 %, nylon ≈ 5–10 %.
field.webbing_weight.label: Webbing weight
field.webbing_weight.help: Weight of the main and backup together, per metre.
field.athlete_mass.label: Walker mass
field.athlete_mass.help: The mass of the walker, with harness and leash.
field.fall_zone.label: Leash fall space
field.fall_zone.help: The free height that must stay below the sagged webbing for a leash fall.
field.source.label: Elevation data
field.source.help: The terrain model for the search. "Automatic" uses the national LiDAR data where we have it, else a Europe-wide model.
field.resolution.label: Grid size
field.resolution.help: The size of one terrain cell. Small cells find small features but the search takes longer. Default: the resolution of the data.
field.water.label: Water surfaces
field.water.help: Gives the sea and lakes a height where the data has none. Then lines over water and edges of sea cliffs are found.
field.coastline.label: Sea outline
field.coastline.help: Where the sea is. OpenStreetMap is the most accurate. The world file is one large download. The Copernicus mask is less accurate (30 m).
field.shore_buffer.label: Shore band
field.shore_buffer.help: Cells without data this near the sea are taken as water.
field.fill_gaps.label: Fill data gaps
field.fill_gaps.help: Fills holes in the terrain data on land from another data set. No anchors are put on the edges of a filled hole.
field.update.label: Check for newer data
field.update.help: Before the search, checks if the stored terrain data has a newer version. "Old only" checks data past its check interval. "All" checks everything.
field.group_distance.label: Group lines with anchors within
field.group_distance.help: Lines whose both anchors are this near become one spot. The map shows one line per spot. You can change it later in the result.
field.group_by.label: Line shown per spot
field.group_by.help: The line that represents a spot on the map.
field.no_html.label: Skip the interactive map
field.no_html.help: Saves the result without the interactive map: only the list of lines as CSV and GeoJSON files.
field.ortho.label: Orthophoto for offline use
field.ortho.help: Stores aerial photo tiles with the result, so the map works without internet. "Automatic" stores them when the download is short, else the map loads them online.
field.ortho_detail.label: Detailed photo around the best spots
field.ortho_detail.help: The number of best spots that get detailed aerial photo tiles. The map loads the detailed photo of the other spots online.
field.threads.label: Threads
field.threads.help: The number of processor threads for the line search. Default: all but one.
field.tile_size.label: Tile size
field.tile_size.help: Large areas are calculated in square tiles. Default: from free memory.
hint.presets.label: Lines to look for
hint.presets.help: A start set for the line length and the anchor height difference. Change the values after you select one.
hint.length.label: Line length
hint.length.help: The distance between the anchors. Use the range of lines that you will rig. A narrow range gives a faster search and a clearer map.
hint.area_name.label: Name of the area
hint.area_name.help: An area from OpenStreetMap: a park, an island, a mountain range. Both anchors of a line are in the area. The webbing can go out of it.
hint.area_file.label: Area file
hint.area_file.help: A GeoJSON, KML or GPX file. Polygons are used as they are. Points and lines get the band width around them.
hint.bounds.factor: On this site: at least {{factor}} × the grid size.

intro.search.title: How a search works
intro.search.what: What it does. The search puts anchors on steep terrain. Then it checks every pair of anchors: the webbing with a walker on it must stay clear of the ground between them. You get the lines that pass.
intro.search.limit_bbox: The whole search fits in a box of {{bbox}} km on each side.
intro.search.limit_active_one: {{count}} search can wait or run at a time.
intro.search.limit_active_other: {{count}} searches can wait or run at the same time.
intro.search.limit_meters: The meters next to your searches show what you used today.
intro.search.narrow: Narrow settings make the search fast. Most settings remove anchors or lines during the search: steepness, prominence, drop, height above the ground, angle to the wall. Fewer anchors means fewer pairs to check. The search ends sooner and the result is easier to read.
intro.search.wide: Wide settings on a large area give too much. A range of 30–2000 m in a large area gives thousands of lines. The search takes long, it can stop at the limit of lines, and the map is full of lines. Start narrow. Make the settings wider only when you get too few lines.
intro.search.example_long: A long line? Do not set 30–2000 m. Set {{length}} 1000–2000 m and {{diff}} 100 m: long lines seldom have anchors at the same height.
intro.search.example_needle: A highline on a rock needle or tower? Set {{length}} 15–60 m, {{prom}} 15 m and {{span}} 40 m. Only anchors on rock that stands out stay.
intro.search.example_exposure: Big exposure over a valley? Set {{height}} 80 m and {{share}} 70 % ({{highAbove}} 20 m). Lines that are high only in the middle are removed.
intro.search.example_sea: Lines straight out from a sea cliff? Use {{cliffs}} → {{coast}}, set {{angle}} 30° and {{drop}} 30 m. The lines leave the wall over the drop, not along it.
intro.search.example_forest: A first highline in a forest area? Use the preset {{preset}} and set {{nmpt}} to {{reject}}. Only lines clear of the trees stay.
intro.result.title: How to read the result
intro.result.spots: Spots and lines. Many found lines are almost the same: their anchors are only a few metres apart. The result puts them together into a spot. The map shows one line for each spot: the line with the most clearance (or the longest or highest, as you select). Select a spot to see all its lines.
intro.result.colour_clean: Pink: the line is clear of the ground.
intro.result.colour_over: Orange: it is clear of the ground but not of trees or buildings.
intro.result.filters: Filters hide lines. Filters do not start a new search. They hide the lines that you do not need, and you can change them at any time. The head of the result shows how many lines the filters hide. Your filters stay in this browser for every result.
intro.result.easy_group: Keep Group similar lines into spots on.
intro.result.easy_within: Increase Anchors within (More filters → Grouping) to put near spots together.
intro.result.easy_clearance: Set Clearance at least 1–2 m: lines that only just pass go away.
intro.result.easy_length: Set Length to the lines that you will rig.
intro.result.easy_spot: Set Lines in a spot at least 3 to see places with many options.
intro.result.easy_off: Turn grouping off only when you look at a small part of the map.
intro.result.check: Check on the spot. The result comes from terrain data. It does not see loose rock, small trees or new buildings, and it does not check a fall onto the backup. Check every line before you rig it.
